To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the stability of pesticides in SPE precolumns is influenced by the storage temperature, 2) the stability of the pesticides in SPE precolumms depends on the chemical structure of the pesticides, and 3) the stability of a pesticide is also influenced by the storage conditions in SPE precolumn.
the stability of four pesticides stored on SPE precolumns is dependent on the type of sorbent and on the storage conditions, but is not affected by the pH of the sample.
the stability of pesticides depends on the chemical nature of the pesticide and on the storage conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of pesticides in SPE precolumns and their storage conditions.
the development of new polymeric sorption materials for the preconcentration of pesticides in ground water and the study of the stability of the pesticides under different storage conditions.
the stability of four pesticides stored on new polymeric SPE cartridges and the comparison of their stability to that stored in C18 cartridges.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stability of pesticides depends on the chemical structure, the pH of the sample, the temperature of storage, the type of precolumn and the type of sorbent.
the use of polymeric precolumns is not recommended in the analysis of fenamiphosphates in ground water samples.
the new polymeric SPE cartridges (IST EnviroLut, LiChrolut and Hysphere-I) are more stable and more efficient than C18 precolumn for the storage of pesticides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new polymeric materials have to be stored in freezer at -20 degrees for at least 1 month to avoid degradation of pesticides.
the stability of pesticides is dependent on the chemical structure of the compounds, the pH and the storage temperature of the water samples and the sorbent material used in the SPE cartridges.
the use of the new polymeric precolumns is recommended for the preconcentration and storage of the four pesticides studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polymeric SPE cartridges are more stable than C18 cartridges when storing pesticides, especially for fenamiphos.
the new polymeric solid-phase sorbents are promising materials for pesticide preconcentration and that the storage of samples in precolumns should be avoided.
SPE cartridges containing the new polymeric material Hysphere-I are more suitable for the storage of pesticides than C18 cartridges.
